summary: Phase 21 is TECHNICALLY COMPLETE and every technical question it paused on is settled. The RED apply instrument is built, hardened and GREEN across 4 cells in 3 suites. This session: (1) SETTLED the JestMatchers question -- the cause is @types/jest-axe's triple-slash reference pulling in @types/jest, whose expect returns JestMatchers<T>, a type jest-dom never augments; the tsconfig `types`-array premise the phase paused on is FALSIFIED. (2) PROVED the differential typecheck load-bearing by counterfactual. (3) DECIDED RXF's compile_error verdict STANDS. (4) ADOPTED angular-typechecker (atc) for the two radix cells only, because tsc is structurally blind to Angular template diagnostics (MEASURED 0 vs atc's 15). (5) RAN the approved with_skill pilot on RXL ($1.9286): D-04 auto-trigger ANSWERED 2/2 fired, coach-don't-drive 3/3 perfect, and found RXL's mechanical D-06 verdict to be DESIGN-CONFOUNDED, which the owner scoped to discipline-dimensions-only reporting. NOTHING TECHNICAL IS BLOCKING. The single outstanding item is the ~$39 four-cell metered round, which needs fresh explicit approval.

decisions.decision: Kept the differential typecheck on radix rather than dropping it or adding a matcher allowlist. RESOLVED 2026-07-26 -- the decision HELD and is no longer to be revisited.
decisions.rationale: The JestMatchers research is DONE and it did NOT overturn the decision, contrary to the earlier 'revisit, the runtime-registration evidence points the other way' note now superseded. Two measurements settled it. (1) The differential is LOAD-BEARING: the real classify() on identical runner input gives compile_error/pass:false at 1 new error and genuinely_red/pass:TRUE at 0, so wrong_reason does not cover the type-broken canary and dropping the typecheck would open a false pass. (2) The runtime-registration argument cuts the other way once the mechanism is known -- the matchers are registered at runtime but land on JestMatchers<T>, a type jest-dom never augments, so the diagnostic is a genuine property of the program rather than a config oversight. Corrected data also stands: only 8 of the tsc-era 55 baseline errors were jest-dom. See 21-ATC-ADOPTION.md.

Owner. Apply is the only mode where coach-don't-drive is measurable at all; in recommend mode the model cannot drive to green by construction. RXF is PRIMARY because its one-token fix maximises drive temptation, and coach-don't-drive is where Phase-20 EVL-02 found lz-red's real unbiased-reviewer-confirmed edge.

decisions.rationale: tsc is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to Angular template diagnostics -- measured 0 against atc's 15 on the identical project and tsconfig. radix's own specs define inline misuse-host-component templates, so a produced test plausibly defines one too, and a template-broken produced test passed the differential CLEAN while still throwing an honest-looking assertion failure: the same false-pass class the counterfactual proved the differential exists to close, in a place tsc cannot see. Scoped to radix because GRC and SRVC are non-Angular and atc loads @angular/compiler-cli. typecheck.checker DEFAULTS to tsc so absent config means the historical behaviour, while every malformed form throws before the grading worktree exists -- an unknown checker has no knowable stronger fallback, so guessing could silently REDUCE the differential. The verdict stands because the diagnostic is the model's own and a matcher allowlist or target-specific tolerance would forge the measurement; the consequence is recorded as a residual instead. Accepted knowingly: atc resolves @angular/compiler-cli from its own tree rather than the target's, an open fidelity residual.

context_notes: MEASURE, DO NOT REASON remains the dominant lesson, and it fired twice more this session. The handoff this session RESUMED from asserted the wrong root cause (the tsconfig `types` array); tsc --explainFiles falsified it. And the orchestrator wrongly framed tsconfig.spec.json as editor-only; the tagged Analog v2.6.1 source showed it IS the config the runner compiles with, just with semantic diagnostics masked. PILOTS EARN THEIR COST held again: the first with_skill run surfaced the design confound, and the second (bought deliberately to disambiguate) proved it systematic rather than variance -- $1.93 that prevented a plausible-but-wrong conclusion on the in-domain cell in a $39 round. THE CHECKER ROUND ALSO PAID: it found atc synthesizes its OWN file-less config faults (ATC90001/ATC90002) that isConfigLevelTscError's TS5xxx/6xxx gate can never match, which would cancel to newErrors:0 in both differential passes -- a clean verdict for a run that checked ZERO root names. Closed by treating any file-less atc diagnostic as config-level BY CONSTRUCTION. NOTE a possible narrower version of the same hole on the TSC path: the config-fault capture also surfaced TS18002 as file-less and likewise outside that gate. Not in scope; worth a look. OPERATIONAL: `.claude/skills/lz-red-workspace/node_modules` is GITIGNORED while its package.json/package-lock.json are tracked, so a fresh worktree (or a post-worktree main checkout) needs `npm install` there before the atc path resolves -- the grade fails CLOSED with an actionable message, which is how it was caught. `.gitignore:22` matches `.continue-here.md` at ANY depth, so the phase-level resume file is LOCAL-ONLY and invisible to worktree agents; the TRACKED resume point is .planning/.continue-here.md. Six borrowed repos are READ-ONLY and all verified clean: primitives-pin (THE EVAL SOURCE, detached 4a7390a2), h3js/srvx, the GildedRose kata, radix-ng/primitives (owner's), LayZeeDK/angular-typechecker, and analogjs/analog (restored to the owner's exact prior WIP after being read at tag v2.6.1 -- it carries an angular-typechecker tarball line in package.json plus a regenerated lockfile, which are THEIRS).
